fatal_errors: The proposed intervention omits the AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating, atmospheric plasma spraying, and the decisive 550 °C post-deposition anneal.
The proposed environments do not reconstruct the reported 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical test or the 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot-corrosion tests.
The sole citation concerns irradiation damage in a W-Ta-V-Cr refractory alloy and provides no support for chromium-oxide passivation or grain-boundary-controlled repassivation in steels.
The experiment changes chromium concentration and grain-boundary structure simultaneously, so it cannot identify which factor governs any corrosion improvement.
explanation: The response addresses the broad corrosion-resistance question and shares part of the target mechanism: chromium-rich passive oxides and microstructural refinement can suppress corrosion. However, it replaces the target system with generic chromium-alloyed steels and misses the APS-deposited AlCoCrFeNi coating, its Al-rich protection, phase structure, coating defects, sluggish-diffusion rationale, and annealing optimum. Its baseline and boundaries are vague and even exclude the high-temperature oxidation regime central to the target. The proposed film-damage measurements could test repassivation, but a factorial design independently varying chromium content and grain-boundary density is required to reveal causality. Most importantly, the cited irradiation study is scientifically irrelevant to the stated passivation hypothesis, leaving the central claims unsupported by the supplied evidence.
